label: EU(7)-PIM: amiodarone, dronedarone
title: Amiodarone or dronedarone in an older person
statement: The EU(7)-PIM list names amiodarone and dronedarone as potentially inappropriate medicines for older people. Amiodarone: it is linked to problems with the QT interval and can provoke torsades de pointes, a dangerous heart rhythm. Dronedarone: it often interacts with other medicines, it lengthens the QT interval, it is not advised when atrial fibrillation is permanent, and deaths from heart and blood vessel causes were more frequent. For both the list adds that, for most older adults, controlling the heart rate gives a better balance of benefit and harm than controlling the heart rhythm. For amiodarone the experts on the list suggest a lower maintenance dose, for example 200 mg every 48 hours. The list states no alternative.

plain_summary: Amiodarone and dronedarone are heart rhythm medicines that can lengthen the QT interval, and the EU(7)-PIM list regards them as potentially inappropriate for an older person. Ask whether the patient still takes the medicine and who reviews it. Ask when they last had an ECG and what they recall about thyroid, liver or lung checks in their monitoring plan.

medicine_groups.name: Amiodarone and dronedarone
medicine_groups.note: Amiodarone may be shown as amiodarone hydrochloride. Tablets and injections count. Amlodipine is a blood pressure medicine with a similar name and does not count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a Group A medicine (amiodarone or dronedarone) is supplied at least once to a person aged 65 or older. If age is missing and the supply otherwise matches, report only a possible finding and ask for age confirmation. A recorded age below 65 is outside scope. One supply is enough, at any dose.
cannot_be_seen: Why the medicine was started and whether a heart specialist chose it. Also ECG results and the QT interval, thyroid, liver and lung checks, potassium and magnesium results, and medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Could you review whether this medicine is still needed and when the last ECG and liver tests were done? For amiodarone, could you also review thyroid and lung monitoring? For dronedarone, could you also review kidney function?
